institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited Hong Kong for a week on holiday a few years prior and decided there that at some point I wanted to live there for a few months. Given that rent is the highest in the world and they have some good universities, I figured that going on exchange and living in a dorm would be my best opportunity to do that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I believe that my exchange was very unique and hard to compare with other exchanges to the same university due to the Covid restrictions.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it was all explained in a single email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved an email containing information about where to be and when.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared dorm rooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of fairly priced canteens on campus, but if you wanted to cook, it was very hard to do so. It did however depend on which dorm you were allocated to, some had kitchens and some didn't.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It won't be the most luxurious place you've ever lived and you will share a room with another exchange student, but seeing as it's only 4 months and that most people are on exchange for the social aspect, it really isn't an issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Information about registration was very messy and vague.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to register on an old and reliable website that the whole school tries to get on at the same time. To make up for this they allow people to register at different times.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful. Nowhere in the information provided to us exchange students did it say that a lot of courses run out of space on the same day you are allowed to register. I starting registering for my courses 2 hours after it opened and 2 of my priority courses were already full so I had to settle for other courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sit ready to register the second they open it up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level was adequate but there was a very big difference from course to course. Some courses I would spend 10 hours a week to prepare for, others I would use 30 minutes max.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It focused a lot on mandatory attendance and weekly assignments, making it feel a lot more like high school than university at UCPH. That doesn't mean the workload is too much though, if you choose "exchange friendly" courses you'll be more than fine.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Topology, Game Theory, Introduction to music theory I, Design and analysis of algorithms and AI ethics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My strongest recommendation would definitely be "Negotiation". Although I didn't have the course myself, I heard from a lot of other exchange students that had that course and they all loved it. It was fun, interactive and the perfect workload to payoff ratio.

Of the courses I myself had I can reccomend game theory, especially seeing as we don't have a similar one back home. It is a fun math courses that gives a very good introduction to the field while clearly showing how applicable it is.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You spend a lot more than you initially budget for on exchange. Although cantines on campus are cheap and there technically are the facilities to cook, you won't have time for that and without noticing you'll be eating out most evenings with your new friends. Bare in mind that these costs are with covid, so given that the nightlife and cultural parts of the cities will be open in the future, expect to spend even more than this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very cheap and convinient but food is more expensive than you think once you leave campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Due to covid there weren't any planned activities yet I've heard from local students that normally exchange students have plenty of acitivies they can sign up to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The campus is heaven for all sport fanatics. It's filled with plenty of sports facilities in perfect condition with a beautiful ocean view.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are also plenty of good hikes around campus that lead to small and cozy beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Due to covid it was never truly necessary. The only true difference was the cuisine, but that was easy to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Due to covid I didn't interact a lot with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. Not many non-student locals spoke english so you had to communicate with your phone quite often but that's about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get a big group of exchange students together and go to
Mr.Wongs
2. Take negotiation as a course, no matter what your major is (unless you are forced to take courses from your faculty of course)
3. Live in the dorms on campus, not in Jockey Hall.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect to spend more than what you budget for, it always costs more than expected.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the other exchange students and having 4 months exploring a new country with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing school work with all the social things you want to do, especially if you study something with a typically high workload.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
